name: Yuki Abara-Szczepański
creator: Yuki Abara-Szczepański
description: Abara-Szczepański works exclusively with language as a physical material — carving, burning, printing, and casting words into surfaces throughout GLMZ in a practice that spans physical installation, illegal public text-works, and meticulously designed physical books produced in editions of fewer than twenty. Her subject is the erosion and mutation of language under corporate standardization: she documents dying idioms, slang, and private family vocabularies gathered through years of Shelf fieldwork, and preserves them in forms designed to outlast the digital. Her book objects are considered among the most significant physical artifacts in contemporary Meridian culture.
medium: physical installation / carved and cast text / physical books / burned surfaces
cultural_impact: Abara-Szczepański's work gave the language-preservation impulse documented in 'Grandmother Tongue' a material, aesthetic form — demonstrating that dying language could be mourned as well as catalogued. Her book objects circulate across all tiers, one of the few cultural artifacts with genuine cross-tier resonance.
controversy: Several corponations whose internal jargon and trademarked terminology appear in her installations have pursued intellectual property claims; she argues that language in common use cannot be owned. One installation was forcibly removed from a Tier 3 corridor after it incorporated unauthorized use of a registered Axiom Media trademark — the word 'Ascend.'
story_hooks: One of Abara-Szczepański's books contains a language documented from a single elderly Shelf resident — and someone who reads it recognizes the vocabulary as belonging to a community that was officially relocated thirty years ago to a place no one can find records of.

She has been commissioned anonymously to document the internal language of a specific corponation's executive tier, with access arranged and payment made — and she cannot determine who hired her or why.
An installation of hers has been modified overnight by an unknown party who added words in a language she does not recognize and cannot place in any of her fieldwork records.
